subject: Post-demo: deployment route & migration checklist (hosted / dedicated / private)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment route & migration checklist (hosted / dedicated / private)

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can scope the next steps: 

Summary from the call:
- Goal: move inference for product search ranking and chat assistant off a brittle internal GPU cluster and reduce per-query cost while meeting PCI/PII controls.
- Traffic profile: ~120QPS peak (batching for ranking), 1–2k users/day for chat, avg prompt length ~600 tokens.

Deployment options we discussed (short pros/cons):
1) Hosted API: fastest to ship, no infra to manage, best for time-to-value but less control for strict egress/compliance.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in our infra. Predictable throughput, can apply private peering and private key control, quicker than full private build.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-controlled network and data plane; best for compliance but requires integration and longer cutover.

Migration sources you mentioned: legacy on-prem GPU cluster + some existing calls to another LLM API. Two clarifying asks so engineering can size the work: 
- Which model backends are you currently running on your cluster (exact checkpoints / formats)?
- Approx size of model artifacts (GBs) and whether you can allow a short secure transfer window for a POC.

Proposed short-term approach:
- Run a 2–3 week Dedicated POC (private peering, reserved capacity) to prove latency and cost targets. If compliance requires, we can then plan a Private deployment cutover.

Next steps (can you confirm in reply):
- Confirm migration source: primarily cluster, primarily external API, or hybrid?
- Procurement contact and preferred PO timeline (if any).
- Available window for a 30–60 minute technical kickoff (I’m proposing Tue 7/20 or Wed 7/21) — meeting link below.

I attached the demo recording and a draft mutual action plan to seed the contract/scoping work. Karthik is cc'd to answer technical sizing questions after your reply.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

soojin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Thanks Jenna — this is perfect context. Answers at a high level and next steps below: 

Pricing / timelines (ballpark):
- Dedicated POC (2–3 weeks): typical POC fee covers reserved GPU hours + engineering onboarding — estimate $18k–30k depending on cluster size and ingress.
- Private VPC/on-prem full cutover: additional engineering (~6–8 weeks) and an onboarding fee; ongoing platform fees apply. We’ll provide a clean SOW once we lock scope.

Private deployment note: Private requires some connectivity/ops work on your side (network peering or air-gapped transfer patterns) but Redwood provides the private control plane and integration helpers; it is not mandatory for you to maintain nodes unless you choose the on-prem flavor.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME migration surface and rough sizing (priv/dedicated)

Internal note — copying my rough engineering assumptions for the kickoff and SOW. Please keep internal: 

- Artifact formats: if their model checkpoints are PyTorch .pt / .bin we can accept direct transfer; for custom runtime coders we’ll need a small conversion step. 300GB model is large but manageable with staged transfer (signed S3 session or physical transfer) for initial ingest.
- Network: for Private VPC we require either direct private peering or an approved egress path; for Dedicated with private peering, we can avoid exposing production data to public internet.
- Migration workstreams and estimates:
  * POC on Dedicated (private peering): 2–3 weeks (1 week infra + 1 week smoke testing + 1 week metrics/runbook verification).
  * Private full cutover (if they want on-prem control): additional 6–8 weeks (integration, KMS/HSM setup, audit controls, latency tuning).
  * Model conversion / compatibility: 3–7 days for standard formats; up to 2–3 weeks if custom runtime ports needed.
- Operational notes: advise the customer to freeze model changes during the POC window; plan for KV cache warm-up to avoid cold-start latency.

Risks / questions to confirm on kickoff:
- Who owns the keys? If they want customer-managed KMS in Private, we need the KMS integration window.
- Data retention / logging requirements: will they require per-tenant log retention >90 days? That affects storage sizing and cost.

Estimated next deliverables from eng: rough SOW line items, POC Sizing Worksheet, and a checklist for secure transfer. I’ll draft the SOW after the 7/20 kickoff.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
